To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the social determinants of health and social emotional wellbeing are important to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island people and should be included in health promotion and prevention activities; 2) Aboriginal and Torres Strait islander peoples' strengths and assets should be incorporated into health and social emotional well-being activities; and 3) the use of a strengths-based approach is an effective way of engaging and empowering Aboriginal and Torres Strait people to take control of their own health and social emotional wellness.

The Aboriginal people in the present study identified a range of factors that they believed contributed to the social and emotional wellbeing of their community, and that these factors were similar to the factors that have previously been reported as contributing to the social and economic wellbeing of Aboriginal people in Australia.

the majority of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Island peoples living in urban areas of Queensland, Australia, perceive their health and wellbeing to be influenced by a range of factors, with social emotional wellbeing and strength-based approaches being particularly salient.
